newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: OVER TWO-THIRDS OF CZECHS WATCH TV NOVA MOST-POLL.
newsitem.headline: OVER TWO-THIRDS OF CZECHS WATCH TV NOVA MOST-POLL.

text.p: Over two-thirds of Czechs said they most often watch the nationwide private station TV Nova, according to a survey conducted by a private poling agency Rapid-DEMA released on Thursday.
The survey at the beginning of the month among 900 Czechs showed 67.8 percent said they watch Nova most often, while 25.9 percent said they watched public station CT1 most frequently.
Private channel TV Premiera, which recenlty changed its name to TV Prima and public station CT2 was favoured by 2.8 and 2.0 percent of the respondents, respectively.
If viewers must choose only one channel to watch with no chance to change the channel for two weeks, 61.1 percent said they would watch Nova, 28.5 CT1, 3.7 TV Premiera and 3.0 CT2.
Nova, launched in February 1994 as the country's first nationwide commercial TV station is majority owned by Central European Median Enterprises Ltd, founded by New York cosmetics heir Ronald Lauder.

The survey also showed the radio station most often listened to is the public station Czech Radiozurnal with 17.6 percent, followed by private station Frekvence 1 at 13.2 percent and Radio Nova Alfa with 9.7 percent.
Fourth was a public station Czech Radio Praha with 8.4 percent. All other radio stations were favoured by less than five percent of listeners.
A question in the survey also focused on the knowledge of exclusive magazines sold in the Czech Republic.
Best known is the Czech edition of Playboy, which is recognised by 78.5 percent of population.
The second one is Penthouse (60.6 pecent), the Czech women's magazine Xantypa (42.4 percent), and the Czech edition of Cosmopolitan (40.3), which has ceased publication.
The Czech women's magazine Betty was next, followed by (39.6) and Czech edition of Elle (32.6).
